content.comment_body: Is it possible to download data without stopping the [article_no] program? The system collects readings from a sensor continuously. Stopping the program risks missing important data. However, I need to download data regularly. Is there any solution to automatically download the data at recurring intervals? I need to retrieve data from about 10 to 20 [article_no] modules daily.

To access a data log, the module must be switched to STOP mode. There isn't another way available. However, you can use programs such as WinMakro to record your steps as a macro and run it at a specific time.

Is there any SDK, API, or protocol documentation explaining how the [product_name] software communicates with the [article_no]? This would allow us to develop our own software instead of relying on macros. Using macros is mainly practical for quick tasks on a local computer. It's difficult to implement on clients' machines without frequent troubleshooting.
From what I know, no such interfaces exist.

analysis.insight_summary: Users face challenges downloading data from the [article_no] module without stopping its program, leading to missed sensor readings. Attempts to automate data downloads across many modules are limited due to the absence of provided APIs, SDKs, or alternative protocols from [company_name]. Workarounds using third-party macro software are regarded as unsuitable for larger, distributed integrations.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope to download logged data without interrupting their running program and preferably automate this process for multiple modules. They also expect official SDKs, APIs, or protocols to enable integration with their own software solutions.
